scope: Current editorial holds only. No decisions, exclusions, owners or manifest changed. Candidate means investigate teachability, not approved lesson.

shortlist.exactSentence: A simple line can land a punch in the final verse.
shortlist.rationale: The boxing-image construction can transfer to a short line, argument or ending that makes a strong impact; the source already applies it to a verse. Keep the unit land a punch with an impact-bearing subject, and test figurative impact rather than literal boxing or generic punch/pack a punch.
shortlist.nearestOwner: Owner 488 punch above its weight concerns unexpectedly strong performance relative to size/resources, not the impact of a particular line.
sevenStepPotential: infer impact from an understated line
reject a merely long or loud line
identify a case with no felt effect
advise a collaborator on a concise final line
use the phrase in another art form
transfer to a different communicative domain
shortlist.gate: Confirm natural register and that six assessments do not collapse into repeated strong-impact paraphrases.

shortlist.exactSentence: Working devices are often thrown aside too quickly.
shortlist.rationale: A separable phrasal verb could teach rejecting a still-useful object prematurely, distinct from systemic throwaway culture. However the complete source is physical disposal while Oxford lists figurative rejection of an attitude or way of life; literal-versus-figurative teachability must be settled before authoring.
shortlist.nearestOwner: Selected throwaway culture (4026) teaches a social habit, not a single disposal decision.
sevenStepPotential: infer premature rejection of usable item
reply about retaining a working tool
write about a different still-useful object
shortlist.gate: Do not draft unless a natural target boundary covering the exact physical source and non-duplicate seven decisions is demonstrated. Oxford sense reference: https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/us/definition/english/throw-aside

explicitlyNotShortlisted.reason: Conventional idiom tighten the screws on someone is coercive pressure on a person; the exact film-silence source is a suspense extension.
